title: Dependency-aware synthesis of current CGT analyses and their generalization boundaries
caption_markdown_lines: **Figure 4 | Dependency-aware synthesis of current CGT analyses and their generalization boundaries.** This figure reorganizes frozen results reported in revised Figures 1–3; it is not an independent replication, validation experiment, or new fitted model. Its upstream universes are distinct and not interchangeable: the META-003 family atlas contains 248 perturbation-response modes from 43 datasets and 9 contexts, grouped into 16 unsupervised families; the PREDICT-003B residual-analysis universe contains 2,720 dataset–perturbation observations from 39 datasets and 8 contexts; and the shared-endpoint fitness benchmark contains 1,229 genes.

**a, Evidence register and permitted claim scope.** Family recurrence is classified as descriptive because the source recurrence score is a run-relative composite rather than a probability, effect size, or transportability estimate. Same-label residual transfer is conditional on the assembled preprocessing and split system: for the context-residual scheme, mean leave-dataset-out cosine is 0.563, falling to 0.035 after exclusion of training datasets with the same study-name proxy. Shared-endpoint fitness prediction is predictive only for the frozen 1,229-gene benchmark: the mean of five held-out-gene fold correlations is \(\bar{\rho}=0.622315\). Candidate pathway coherence is post hoc and study-conditioned: nine manually curated candidate annotations are displayed, with maximum dominant-study-proxy shares from 0.643 to 1.000. A causal mechanism is classified as not tested because no prospective intervention or external-study mechanism experiment was performed. These rows reuse analyses and are neither independent replications nor a validation ladder.

**b, Study-conditioned candidate summaries.** Rows are three manually designated headline (`H`) and six supporting (`S`) candidate annotation groups from revised Figure 3; these tiers are curation labels, not calibrated evidence grades. Columns report the maximum source recurrence score \(R_f\), corrected ORA and rank-analysis \(-\log_{10}(q)\), maximum absolute standardized RidgeCV coefficient \(|\beta|\), maximum absolute high-confidence Spearman association \(|\rho|\), and maximum dominant-study-proxy share across each group’s constituent family or query views. ORA and rank \(q\) values were Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted separately across the 201,771 corrected view–term tests per method in Figure 3; `NR` means no retained rank result, not zero. The ORA and rank columns reuse the same residual coordinates and overlapping gene-set memberships. The \(|\beta|\) and \(|\rho|\) columns reuse the same DepMap-derived essentiality-strength endpoint; \(\beta\) is also coding- and penalty-dependent because the closed 16-feature matrix has rank 12. Values are maxima, have unlike units, and are not commensurate. Cell shade is normalized separately within each column and does not define a combined evidence score. Seven of the nine displayed groups have maximum study-proxy share 1.000; the chromatin/epigenetic group has 0.875 and the antigen-receptor/tolerance group 0.643. Candidate labels are manually curated, study-conditioned shorthand rather than validated biological axes or mechanisms.

**c, Raw-metric atlas.** The numbered groups from panel b are plotted without a composite score, bubble-size encoding, or displacement of measured coordinates. The upper track shows \(R_f\) against maximum \(|\beta|\); the lower track shows \(R_f\) against maximum \(|\rho|\). Filled symbols denote headline groups and open symbols supporting groups. Candidate 2 is drawn as a smaller filled diamond at its exact coordinates in both tracks. In the upper \(|\beta|\) track, its marker overlaps the footprint of the larger open `4/6` marker; in the lower \(|\rho|\) track, the values are vertically distinct. Leader lines identify candidate 2 without moving either measured coordinate. Groups 4 and 6 are both F10-linked summaries and have exactly the same plotted values—\(R_f=2.92019\), \(|\beta|=0.03509\), and \(|\rho|=0.13472\)—so they share one open symbol labelled `4/6` in each track, rather than being separated by artificial jitter. No uncertainty interval is available for these descriptive maxima.

**d, Generalization boundaries.** The left track shows same-label transfer for the context-residual coordinate scheme. Diamonds are observation-weighted mean cosines and horizontal bars are percentile 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals from 4,000 resamples: leave-dataset-out, 0.56320 [0.36897, 0.79476; 34 held-out datasets, 1,092 finite rows]; exclusion of training datasets sharing the held-out dataset’s string-prefix study proxy, 0.03500 [−0.03730, 0.09316; 22 held-out datasets, 507 finite rows]; and leave-context-out, 0.07937 [0.04801, 0.12778; 7 held-out contexts, 496 finite rows]. “Study proxy” is not verified study identity. Residual baselines were estimated from the full PREDICT-003B table before splitting, so these results are conditional on transductive preprocessing rather than a fully nested inductive pipeline. The right track shows every available regression-Spearman replicate from the shared-endpoint fitness analysis; small circles are raw replicate estimates and diamonds their means. Means and replicate counts are held-out gene, 0.62232 (\(n=5\) folds); program family, 0.12680 (\(n=7\)); dataset, 0.09192 (\(n=5\)); context, −0.05478 (\(n=4\)); and study proxy, −0.14224 (\(n=5\)). These counts are available fold- or group-level replicate summaries, not gene counts. The residual and fitness tracks have different estimands, scales, denominators, and resampling units and are not quantitatively pooled.

**e, Scoped model and decisive falsifiers.** The schematic summarizes an explicitly limited interpretation: residual coordinates recur in related settings but depend on preprocessing; transfer attenuates and candidate annotations concentrate by study or context; held-out genes predict a shared endpoint, whereas grouped estimates are unstable. Arrows organize this descriptive sequence and do not represent a fitted or causal model. A `STOP` barrier separates shared-endpoint prediction from a causal-law claim. Broader claims would require fold-fitted preprocessing, verified study identifiers, independent-study recurrence, a declared contrast basis, study-block uncertainty, and prospective mechanism or intervention tests. The figure therefore supports a dependency-aware synthesis of within-pipeline structure, study-conditioned annotation, and retrospective prediction; it does not establish independent biological replication, context-general transport, universal axes, mechanism, or a causal constraint law.
alt: Five-panel synthesis of CGT evidence and its limits. Nine post hoc candidate annotations are strongly study-conditioned; residual transfer and fitness association attenuate under harder study-proxy, context, and grouped holdouts. A final `STOP` barrier marks a universal causal law as untested.
accessible_description_markdown_lines: Figure 4 is a vertically arranged five-panel figure on a white background. It summarizes earlier analyses rather than adding independent evidence.

Panel a is a four-column register with five rows. Descriptive family recurrence comprises 248 modes, 43 datasets, 9 contexts, and 16 unsupervised families and is run-relative rather than a transportability estimate. Conditional same-label residual transfer has leave-dataset cosine 0.563 and same-study-proxy-exclusion cosine 0.035; broad transport is not established. Predictive shared-endpoint fitness analysis has mean fold Spearman correlation 0.622 across five folds in a 1,229-gene benchmark; grouped holdouts are unstable. Post hoc pathway coherence displays nine candidate annotations with maximum dominant-study-proxy shares from 0.643 to 1.000. Causal mechanism is marked not tested because no prospective intervention or external-study mechanism test was performed.

Panel b is a nine-row numeric matrix. The rows, followed by recurrence score, ORA \(-\log_{10}(q)\), rank \(-\log_{10}(q)\), maximum \(|\beta|\), maximum \(|\rho|\), and maximum study share, are: 1, Cytokine/JAK–STAT: 12.65, 54.7, 16.0, 0.023, 0.291, 1.000; 2, Chromatin/epigenetic: 2.86, 14.5, `NR`, 0.029, 0.020, 0.875; 3, Translation/RQC: 1.85, 9.9, 21.1, 0.249, 0.156, 1.000; 4, Chromatin–cytokine: 2.92, 39.0, 21.5, 0.035, 0.135, 1.000; 5, OXPHOS/TCA: −3.54, 8.9, 11.1, 0.101, 0.441, 1.000; 6, Lysosome/ECM: 2.92, 5.3, 4.3, 0.035, 0.135, 1.000; 7, rRNA biogenesis: 1.05, 4.3, 3.3, 0.039, 0.032, 1.000; 8, SREBP/cholesterol: −2.25, 6.1, 5.1, 0.037, 0.044, 1.000; and 9, Antigen-receptor/tolerance: −2.56, 3.1, 3.6, 0.028, 0.037, 0.643. Darker shading marks larger values within each column only. ORA and rank reuse the same residual coordinates; \(|\beta|\) and \(|\rho|\) reuse the same DepMap endpoint.

Panel c contains two small scatterplots sharing the run-relative recurrence score \(R_f\). The upper vertical axis is maximum \(|\beta|\); the lower is maximum \(|\rho|\). Filled symbols identify headline groups and open symbols supporting groups. Candidate 2 is a smaller filled diamond at its exact coordinates in both tracks. It overlaps the larger open `4/6` marker footprint only in the upper \(|\beta|\) track; the lower \(|\rho|\) values are vertically distinct. Thin leader lines identify candidate 2 without displacement. Groups 4 and 6 occupy exactly the same point in both plots and are labelled together as `4/6`. Group 1 lies farthest right because its recurrence score is 12.65. Group 3 has the largest \(|\beta|\), 0.249, and group 5 the largest \(|\rho|\), 0.441.

Panel d contains two side-by-side boundary plots. The left plot shows mean context-residual transfer: leave-dataset-out, 0.563 with 95% cluster interval 0.369 to 0.795; exclude same-study proxy, 0.035 with interval −0.037 to 0.093; and leave context out, 0.079 with interval 0.048 to 0.128. Cluster counts are 34, 22, and 7. The right plot shows raw Spearman replicates as small grey circles and means as purple diamonds. Means are 0.622 for five gene folds, 0.127 for seven program-family estimates, 0.092 for five dataset estimates, −0.055 for four context estimates, and −0.142 for five study-proxy estimates. The two tracks are not on a shared quantitative scale.

Panel e is a four-card schematic. Residual coordinates recur in related settings but are preprocessing-dependent; study/context conditioning attenuates transfer and concentrates candidate labels; shared-endpoint prediction works for held-out genes while grouped estimates are unstable. An orange barrier labelled `STOP` separates these cards from a causal-law card stating that no prospective mechanism or intervention test exists. Broader claims require fold-fitted preprocessing, verified study IDs, independent-study recurrence, a declared contrast basis, study-block uncertainty, and prospective mechanism or intervention tests.
